subject: Token spend snapshot + approval gate questions
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Clara Hughes <clara.hughes@orchard.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T10:03:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + a couple procurement questions

Hi Clara —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Short recap and two clarifying questions for procurement so we can put together a clean PO path:  

Recap:
- Primary use: customer-facing summarization + vector search augmentation.
- Traffic profile (est): 100k–400k prompt tokens/day during pilot; peaks on month-end reporting windows.
- Desired SLA: 99.9% uptime, <150ms p95 for short-form responses.

Questions for procurement: 
1) What monthly spend band should we qualify for internal approvals today? (e.g., <$5k/mo, $5k–$25k, $25k–$100k, >$100k) — this determines whether they need a simple PO vs. procurement committee signoff.
2) Does Orchard have a PO/contract threshold (USD) above which legal needs to review or additional finance signatures are required? Also any standard lead times we should budget for?

We want to propose a couple of committed bands with target unit economics to hit your preferred price point. If you can confirm the procurement threshold and expected monthly corridor, I’ll send a short spreadsheet with three commit scenarios and the corresponding $/1M token targets for each.

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
m: +1 (415) 555-0124
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: none in this message
From: Clara Hughes <clara.hughes@orchard.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-13T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple procurement questions

Thanks Markus — great summary. A few answers from procurement side:  

- Expected monthly spend (pilot): roughly $7k–$18k depending on model mix and caching behavior. Production could expand to $40k–$120k/mo within 6–9 months if adoption goes well.
- PO/approval thresholds: Our finance team handles up to $25k/month with a standard PO (no extra legal review). Anything over $25k requires a procurement committee review and a VP of Finance signoff; contracts >$75k typically go to legal for additional terms.
- Lead time: Standard PO review is ~3 business days; procurement committee schedules weekly but expect 7–10 business days for approvals once submitted.

A couple of asks from our side: please include an outline for minimum commit vs. burst pricing, and a target $/1M-token rate for each spend band. Would also be helpful to see a quick sensitivity table that maps 3 usage profiles to expected monthly dollar spend (to help justify band selection internally).

I can loop in procurement@orchard.ai if you want them on the thread.

Regards,
Clara
Clara Hughes
Director, Growth & Partnerships — Orchard AI
clara.hughes@orchard.ai

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Clara Hughes <clara.hughes@orchard.ai>, Orchard AI Procurement <procurement@orchard.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T15:26:00Z
Subject: Proposed spend bands + unit economics (spreadsheet attached)

Hi Clara / procurement team —

Per Clara’s note, attaching a short spreadsheet (orchard-pricing-breakdown.xlsx) with three proposed commit bands and the expected $/1M-token equivalent we can hit if Orchard chooses the corresponding reserved capacity/commit approach. Highlights below:  

- Band A (pilot): $6k–$20k/mo — target $/1M tokens: $850–$1,200 (no long-term commit, use-hosted with modest prefix caching)
- Band B (growth): $20k–$60k/mo — target $/1M tokens: $420–$700 (3–6 month commit recommended; improved batching & partial cache reserved)
- Band C (enterprise): $60k+/mo — target $/1M tokens: $180–$360 (12-month reserved capacity, advanced quantization + caching)

Procurement notes: 
- For PO guidance, we typically see customers route Band A with standard PO (sub-$25k) and Band B requires procurement committee review in your org (as you noted). Band C typically needs legal and VP-level approvals.
- Lead times: allow 3–10 business days for PO signoff depending on band; legal review adds 7–14 business days.

Actions I’ll take next:
1) Upload the spreadsheet to the Drive link and share with procurement.
2) Draft a plain-language pricing summary you can attach to the PO to speed approvals.
3) If you confirm which band to qualify for internally, we’ll produce a short SOW + PO-ready invoice.

Laura — looping you for any additional finance notes on invoicing terms (net-30 vs net-45) or required billing contact. Karthik — appreciate a quick sanity check on the unit economics above before I share externally.

Thanks,
Markus

Attachments: orchard-pricing-breakdown.xlsx
From: Clara Hughes <clara.hughes@orchard.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Orchard AI Procurement <procurement@orchard.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Proposed spend bands + unit economics (spreadsheet attached)

Markus / team —

This is helpful — thanks for putting the bands together. Procurement will qualify us for Band B for the pilot review (i.e., we should budget as though we’re in the $20k–$60k/mo corridor for approvals). A few quick clarifications before I route to the committee:  

- For Band B, can you confirm the minimum monthly commit (if any) that unlocks the $420 figure?
- We’ll need the PO-ready summary you mentioned (short plain-language doc) and a sample invoice with line items (tokens, storage, optional observability add-on). If possible, send the sample invoice as a PDF so procurement can attach directly to the PO request.
- Procurement also asked whether we can include automatic fallback to a cheaper compatible model in case of capacity constraints (they want this in writing in the SOW).

If you can share: the minimum commit number for Band B, the sample invoice PDF, and the SOW line about fallback behavior, I’ll submit to committee next week.

Clara

Clara Hughes
Director, Growth & Partnerships — Orchard AI
clara.hughes@orchard.ai
